name: Shoulder Impingement Syndrome / Subacromial Pain Syndrome
tags: shoulder impingement syndrome / subacromial pain syndrome
definition: Clinical syndrome of shoulder pain related to rotator cuff/subacromial structures, best understood as a symptom-based diagnosis rather than simple mechanical 'impingement'.

typical: Rotator cuff weakness may be pain-limited

investigations.principle: Imaging is not routinely needed initially; ultrasound/MRI is used for persistent symptoms or suspected tear.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, physeal, occult injury, deformity or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Avoid over-reliance on isolated provocative tests or imaging morphology.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-Snayu pain phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Clinical syndrome of shoulder pain related to rotator cuff/subacromial structures, best understood as a symptom-based diagnosis rather than simple mechanical 'impingement'.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, open injury, severe deformity, rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, suspected infection or other listed red flags.

sources.title: Rotator Cuff Related Shoulder Pain resources
